**MiMo-V2.6-Pro is the stronger model. GPT-6 Luna is the cheaper, much faster one.** They are not peers: Luna is OpenAI’s low-cost GPT-6 tier, while Xiaomi’s Pro is the current top open-weight model and sits well above Luna on independent intelligence scores.

Both shipped in the same week (around 22 September 2026). Neither is a frontier flagship. On Artificial Analysis, Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra sit at 53, and Claude Opus 5.5 higher still. MiMo-V2.6-Pro is at 46, first among open-weight models. GPT-6 Luna (high) is at 32.[1][2]

## Scores

| | GPT-6 Luna (high) | MiMo-V2.6-Pro |
|---|---|---|
| AA Intelligence Index | 32 | **46** |
| AA-Briefcase v1.1 | 1176 | **1517** |
| GDPval-AA v2.1 | 1290 | **1673** |
| AutomationBench-AA | 48% | **59%** |
| Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 5% | **35%** |
| SciCode | 50% | **61%** |
| Humanity’s Last Exam | 33% | **49%** |
| AA-Omniscience | −6 | **8** |
| AA-LCR v1.1 | 79% | **86%** |

MiMo wins every shared row in that Artificial Analysis head-to-head. The gap is widest on terminal and agent work: 35% vs 5% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and 59% vs 48% on AutomationBench-AA.[1]

LLM Stats puts them closer on its own composite (MiMo 49.9, Luna 44.5) and gives MiMo the edge on reasoning, coding, agents, and tool use. In the three exact shared benchmarks it tracks, MiMo wins AutomationBench and DeepSWE; Luna wins Agents’ Last Exam.[3]

Vision is the exception. On Roboflow Vision Evals, Luna averages 68.6% against MiMo’s 62.5%, and leads 4 of 6 tasks. The biggest gap is visual reasoning: 52.1% vs 35.1%.[4]

## Price and speed

| | GPT-6 Luna | MiMo-V2.6-Pro |
|---|---|---|
| Input / 1M | **$0.10** | $0.435 |
| Output / 1M | **$0.50** | $0.87 |
| Cache hit / 1M | $0.01 | **$0.0036** |
| Blended price / 1M | **$0.077** | $0.177 |
| Cost per AA task | **$0.03** | $0.13 |
| Output speed | **149 tok/s** | 42 tok/s |
| Time to first answer token | **5.77s** | 50.93s |
| Time per AA task | **133s** | 1,474s |
| Output tokens per task | **20k** | 64k |

Luna is about 4.3× cheaper on input and 1.7× cheaper on output. MiMo’s cache hits are nearly free ($0.0036 vs $0.01), so long repeated prompts narrow the gap, but Luna still wins on cost per task because it writes far fewer tokens.[5][1]

Speed is not close. Luna generates about 149 tokens per second and starts answering in under 6 seconds. MiMo’s first token arrives faster (3.45s), then it thinks: first answer token at about 51 seconds, and an end-to-end 500-token reply around 63 seconds versus Luna’s 9 seconds.[1]

## What they actually are

MiMo-V2.6-Pro is a sparse mixture-of-experts model: about 1.02 trillion total parameters, 42 billion active, 1 million-token context, MIT license, weights on Hugging Face. It takes text, image, video, and audio, and returns text. Self-hosting the flagship is a data-center job (about 566 GB of MXFP4 weights, eight or more GPUs). Xiaomi also ships a cheaper Flash tier and a 9B distill.[6][7]

GPT-6 Luna is proprietary, API-only, with a 1,050,000-token input window and a 128,000-token output cap. Documented knowledge cutoff is 18 May 2026. It is the efficiency model in the GPT-6 line, not Astra.[3][5]

A same-prompt DevOps check (Kubernetes, bash backup script, Terraform, nine calls each) is a useful reality check. Both passed bash and `tofu validate` on every run. Both mostly failed a live nginx manifest that asked for a non-root user: Luna 0 of 3 HTTP 200, MiMo Pro 1 of 3. Luna did it for $0.0036 and 6,936 output tokens; MiMo cost $0.017 and used 18,867 tokens. Linters passed manifests that then crash-looped.[6]

## Which to use

- **MiMo-V2.6-Pro** when quality, coding agents, open weights, or self-hosting matter, and you can wait and review the output. It is also the one seeing heavy real traffic: about 1.07 trillion tokens on OpenRouter in the latest rankings.[8]
- **GPT-6 Luna** when you need cheap, fast volume: chat, classification, short coding help, or agent loops where latency and token cost dominate. It is also the better of the two on Roboflow’s vision suite.[4]
- **Neither** if the job has to be right without a checker. In that DevOps test, GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 were the ones that passed every runtime check.[6]

If you are choosing an API default in Budapest and the workload is mixed, Luna is the sane cheap default and MiMo Pro is the model to route hard agent or code tasks to.
